The line is dark and jagged with no discontinuity and no second light, so CT-1 cannot be satisfied and shadow cannot be ruled out or confirmed. PROC-CT-003 would call a crack after one lighting change, but it conflicts with the more specific and demanding CT-1, which requires two lights, an oblique_low discontinuity and a reference comparison, so I follow CT-1. Also, the line is jagged and roughly vertical, not a straight horizontal line, and a single image does not meet even that rule's one-lighting-change requirement. PROC-CT-002 (crazing) does not fit because the finding is a single dominant line, not a cobweb network. A jagged path alone is not proof. The evidence is insufficient.

PROC-CT-002 does not apply: the finding is a single dominant line, not a crazing network.

get_reference {'category': 'ceramic_tile'}: Conditions 1 and 2 of CT-1 are already met (line fixed across two lights at front pose; discontinuity at oblique_low). The only missing piece for a verdict is condition 3: whether the line is absent on the approved reference tile. Camera moves to left_45/right_45/top add views but do not resolve the reference question. get_reference is the only action that directly separates a genuine tile crack from an artifact present on the tile design. | expects: If the jagged vertical line is a real crack in this tile, the approved defect-free reference tile should show no such line at the same position (matches_reference false for the line, completing CT-1 condition 3, which would support Suspected defect given conditions 1 and 2 already hold). If the line is a drawn mark, stain, hair or other surface artifact that also appears on the reference or is a feature of the reference, the reference would show a similar line, or the defect verdict would be undermined. A reference image with no line at this position supports a genuine crack; a reference with the same line indicates it is not a tile defect.
